dialect.guess: IBM Enterprise COBOL or compatible (likely NEC/Fujitsu mainframe or GnuCOBOL on Linux, given JMA ORCA project context)
evidence: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION / ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / DATA DIVISION / PROCEDURE DIVISION all present
SELECT ... ASSIGN ... ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED / ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC / RECORD KEY / FILE STATUS
COPY with REPLACING using // delimiters (Micro Focus / GnuCOBOL style)

purpose.summary: This program is part of the JMA (Japan Medical Association) ORCA open-source medical receipt (claims) software. It creates print files for medical insurance receipts (レセプト印刷用ファイル作成), specifically handling the 2003/April revision and later amendments for health insurance billing. It reads multiple indexed receipt data files, processes insurance history, benefit ratios, and customization items, and produces output for receipt printing.

notable_features: Multiple indexed VSAM-style files with DYNAMIC access mode
Extensive use of COPY with REPLACING (// delimiter style, Micro Focus/GnuCOBOL convention)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS (pure file-based I/O)
111 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprogram calls
Japanese comments encoded in latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, decoded as latin-1 causing mojibake)
Copyright JMA 2002, open-source medical receipt software (ORCA project)
No COMP-3 usage despite financial/billing domain
verdict.notes: The file is decoded as latin-1 but the Japanese comments are almost certainly EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, causing the garbled appearance. The COPY delimiter style (//) is characteristic of Micro Focus COBOL or GnuCOBOL. The ORCA project (JMA standard receipt software) is a well-known open-source Japanese medical billing system, confirming production-grade code. No COMP-3 is unusual for a financial application but consistent with the indicators.
